system: You are a security investigator reviewing an alert. Base every claim only on the evidence available to you. Cite the record IDs that support each observation.

supporting_observations.claim: The supplied endpoint process records do not show PowerShell starting around the reported 13:40 time. They do show a PowerShell process started at 14:16:52 under maria.lopez, at medium integrity, running `Invoke-WebRequest` against the NuGet API; it exited about 11 seconds later.

At 13:44, the proxy recorded a successful GET for `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/harbor-dental-it/tools/main/u.ps1`, with no user-agent recorded for that GET. The records do not identify the initiating process or establish what the downloaded script contained or whether it ran.

The workstation made Kerberos and LDAP requests to the domain controller around 13:40; the records attribute the relevant traffic to LSASS and show machine-account authentication. These records do not establish that PowerShell caused the activity.

The workstation made SMB connections to the domain controller at 13:49 and 14:12, authenticated as its machine account. The available records show connection-level activity, not which shares or files were accessed.
The evidence is insufficient to determine whether the GitHub script download, the reported PowerShell window, and the later NuGet request were related or malicious.

known_telemetry_limitations: The supplied records do not include evidence identifying which process initiated the GitHub request or the contents or hash of the downloaded script.
No PowerShell script-block or equivalent execution-content records are supplied, so the commands or scripts run near 13:40 cannot be determined from this evidence.
The SMB records show connections but not share names, file operations, or accessed content.
The supplied records are a limited set of events; absence of a process-start record around 13:40 does not establish that no PowerShell window appeared.
claims_not_established: Whether PowerShell actually appeared at the reported 13:40 time.
Whether the downloaded `u.ps1` was executed, and, if so, what it did.
Whether the GitHub download and the later PowerShell NuGet request were related.
Whether the SMB connections accessed files or shares, or were authorized activity.
Whether the observed activity was malicious or benign.
additional_evidence_needed: Collect complete endpoint process, PowerShell, and file-creation telemetry for WS-MLOPEZ-01 from 13:20 to 14:20 UTC, including script-block logs if available.
Retrieve the proxy response body or a preserved copy and hash of `u.ps1`, and identify the process responsible for requesting it.
Review browser download history and endpoint file-system artifacts for the script and related files.
Obtain SMB share-access and file-operation logs for the workstation's connections to DC-HD-01.
Check with IT whether the GitHub repository, script, and observed activity were authorized or connected to planned work.
